categories.name: Financial Sustainability
evidence: Up to ~$600k damage cost to buildings in area (moderate)
Up to ~$110k damage to selected key road segments (minor)
categories.tolerance: Council tolerates likely financial impacts of up to $20K or 2% of their annual budget. Financial impacts (expenditure or revenue) of up to $5M or 50% of the annual budget may be accepted for strategic initiatives or transformative projects.

categories.name: Core Service Delivery / Asset Management
evidence: Council facility (civic centre, YMCA, community centre) impacted two weeks (minor)
Temporary impact on compliance, service KPIs or vulnerable populations; may require management intervention (moderate)
Woodville Oval Croquet Clubrooms affected up to one month (moderate)
Roads near The Queen Elizabeth Hospital could be closed for 3 days
categories.tolerance: Council does not tolerate likely impacts on Council facilities lasting more than one month or delays in infrastructure project milestones exceeding three months.

categories.name: Legislative / Regulatory
evidence: Exposure of critical infrastructure and essential services, including the hospital (S1), railway station (S3), power substation (S6) and major arterial roads (A1–A3)
categories.tolerance: Council does not tolerate any likely breaches of a technical nature or any litigation or court proceedings.

categories.name: Reputation
evidence: Disrupted access to The Queen Elizabeth Hospital (S1) through Woodville Rd, Woodville South (A1, 0.10–0.20 m)
Aged care residents may need evacuation or face disrupted care (S4, S5)
Woodville Primary School closure (S2) and disruption at the Woodville rail junction (S3)
Port Rd (A3, 0.20–0.50 m), the direct route to the Royal Adelaide Hospital, partly unsafe for vehicles, causing congestion across the network
categories.tolerance: Council does not tolerate likely repeated negative national or state media coverage lasting several months, a successful vote of no confidence, or the forced resignation or government investigation of the CEO, Mayor or councillors. Negative media coverage lasting more than 30 days, large-scale campaigns or petitions may be tolerated in limited circumstances where key strategic outcomes can be achieved or differing community views need to be balanced.

categories.name: Our People
evidence: Crews doing traffic control and clean-up next to flooded arterials (A1, A3)
Access to civic facilities restricted on Woodville Rd (A2, 0.02–0.05 m)
More demand on relief-centre staff and volunteers
categories.tolerance: Council does not tolerate any likely near-miss incidents. Council tolerates annual permanent staff and volunteer turnover of up to 10%.

categories.name: Environment
evidence: Hydrocarbons, litter and sediment washed off Port Rd and Woodville Rd into the stormwater network
Reserves (St Clair Recreation Ground, Woodville Park) temporarily closed
categories.tolerance: Likely temporary environmental impacts lasting up to one month (reversible impacts), potentially affecting multiple sites but remaining localised.

categories.name: Community Wellbeing and Local Economy
evidence: Delays for ambulances, patient transport and hospital staff getting to S1
Disrupted care for aged care residents (S4, S5), made worse if a substation outage (S6) cuts power to medical equipment or cooling
Lost school days (S2)
Rail commuters displaced (S3); freight and commuter delays on Port Rd (A3)
Lost trade for businesses along Woodville Rd and Port Rd
categories.tolerance: Council does not tolerate any likely decrease in the use of community facilities (libraries, halls, community centres, reserves and sporting grounds) or any direct impacts on community members' safety.
